    "Revenue recovery driven by Indian Railways capex ramp-up: FY2021 revenues declined ~7.8% YoY (Net Revenue from Operations fell from ~INR 1,832 Cr to ~INR 1,689 Cr) due to COVID-19 disruptions to wagon orders and EPC execution; we assume mean-reversion toward a ~13% CAGR in FY2022 and ~12-13% thereafter, anchored by the Government of India's continued thrust on railway infrastructure spending and Texmaco's dominant market position in freight wagons and rail EPC.",
    "Net Profit margin remains thin but improves gradually: FY2021 PAT attributable to owners was ~INR 14 Cr (INR 1,416 lakhs) on a very low base after an exceptional-loss-impacted FY2020 (PAT of negative INR 6,483 lakhs); the company carries high leverage (short-term borrowings ~INR 727 Cr, total borrowings ~INR 763 Cr vs equity ~INR 1,141 Cr) and elevated finance costs (~INR 103 Cr), constraining margin expansion; we assume gradual PAT improvement as revenue scales and working capital normalises, but do not forecast aggressive margin recovery given leverage and competitive EPC segment dynamics."
  ],
  "reasoning": "FY2021 is anomalous: Net Revenue from Operations fell ~7.8% YoY to INR 1,689 Cr (INR 168,885 lakhs converted at INR 1 lakh = INR 0.01 Cr, i.e. ~INR 1,689 Cr) from INR 1,832 Cr in FY2020, driven by COVID-19 disruptions to manufacturing, order execution, and Railways procurement timelines \u2014 making the latest year's growth rate unreliable as a projection basis. Only two years of P&L data are available in the report (FY2020 and FY2021), so a multi-year CAGR cannot be computed from the text alone; instead, we rely on the known structural growth driver (Indian Railways multi-year capex program, National Rail Plan targeting INR 50 lakh crore investment) and assume recovery toward a ~12-13% revenue CAGR over FY2022-24, consistent with the company's historical wagon order pipeline and EPC segment expansion. Net Profit forecasts are kept conservative given the high debt burden (~INR 763 Cr total borrowings), elevated finance costs (~INR 103 Cr per annum), and thin operating leverage in the near term; EPS is computed on a diluted share base of approximately 25.03 crore shares (equity share capital INR 2,503 lakhs at face value INR 1 each)."
}

Step 2: For each assumption, describe one plausible scenario where it fails.
Step 3: Rate each assumption failure as Low / Medium / High risk to the forecast accuracy.
Step 4: Assign an overall confidence score from 0-100 (100 = completely certain).
